title: The role of negative affect regulation in the maintenance of restriction in anorexia nervosa spectrum disorders.
abstract: Restriction is a core behavioral symptom of anorexia nervosa spectrum disorders (ANSD), including anorexia nervosa (AN) and atypical AN (AAN). Emotion regulation theories of eating pathology posit that restriction and restraint are maintained via their influence on affective processes, but prior research has not firmly established the affect regulatory role of restriction and restraint. Using 30 days of ecological momentary assessment data collected from 83 adults with ANSD (AN = 47, AAN = 36), we specified a series of dynamic structural equation models to clarify the temporal interplay between restriction/restraint and negative affect. We also tested whether the relationship between restriction/restraint and negative affect was moderated by diagnosis (i.e., AN vs. AAN). Group-level analyses suggested inconsistent effects of restriction and restraint on affect, whereas increases in negative affect reliably predicted restriction and restraint. However, there was considerable idiographic heterogeneity in cross-lagged effects across models. Temporal dynamics between restriction/restraint and affect did not systematically differ as a function of diagnosis. Although restriction and restraint may provide relief from negative affect for many individuals, the present findings suggest that they may not serve a universal or lasting affect regulatory function in ANSD. These results underscore the importance of idiographic approaches to eating disorder research and treatment. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).
